# the contributor audit: the explicit same-separator cone applies at selected minima

Source: `candidate 9158d8d941246660`.
Full read, Sections 1--7: PASS in the established compact cardinality-minimal
bad-base framework. Defect's independent complete audit also passes.

## 1. Full-parameter cover and its finite contacts

The positive weighted geometric mean gives joint concavity of
f=M^(-1/N)L^(1/N)F^(d/N), and strict own-fiber concavity follows from that
of F. The superdifferential calculation handles a prescribed fiber gradient
at a PL crease: it is the corresponding combination of active L-plane
gradients plus the unique energy-root gradient. Extending those two parts
separately gives precisely the full tangent required by the old cover proof.

Uniform own properness and the atomic gap are prior geometric results, so
compact-tilt selection supplies actual mass-Q caps. The fixed-face parity
argument applies to conv(I), and every assigned integer base has a zero
contact. Strict own concavity rules out both a second interior zero and an
additional boundary zero. Thus the finite contact hypothesis, including one
mark per assigned base, is actually verified here rather than assumed.

## 2. Actual signed normal-dependent deformations

For each unit normal u the displayed inequalities u.x+t Phi(u,z,x)<=h_z(u)
define convex fibers. Uniform convex lower linear bounds first bound the
new bodies; on that bounded region Phi is bounded, giving inner homothetic
and outer parallel bounds. Jensen and the original anchored support
inequalities verify every compatibility inclusion exactly. The canonical
hull therefore has the intended sampled fibers.

At a regular old radial endpoint the unique active normal identifies the
signed first speed Phi(n,z,x). The uniform radial bound permits the signed
shell expansions even at nonsmooth bodies. Continuous fields are continuous
on each supporting facet, as needed by the all-status hinge response.
Finite sums remain actual, and signed normal-dependent affine fields are
included. This is the archived normal-bundle cone, not every formal array.

The simultaneous parameter directions are concave and positive on the
nearby actual bodies for small t. Their normalization expansion uses the
old zero logarithmic mean, so there is no omitted derivative of its volume
denominator. No derivative of a reoptimized parameter is assumed.

## 3. Contact budgets, nonsmooth responses, and one dual

The coefficient (12) has all required signs: energy C_E/(NE), covariance
J/(2M), total-volume term -(N+2)D/(2NM), logarithmic boundary term -s_L/N,
raw marked parameter term -h/(NL), normalization H/N, and scalar term -s.
Uniform expansions localize the minimum to the entire finite contact set.
The exact quantile equation covers each assigned current fiber and the
strict gaps cover all other bases. These are actual global comparisons.

Dropping only the positive inside hinge gives a concave sufficient-descent
response while retaining full inside body loss. Outside selectors remain
jointly fixed with their coareas and moments. Compact finite-intersection
selection yields ONE separator for all normal-dependent convex fields, the
parameter class, cap-normal controls and both logarithmic-scale signs.

Accordingly the former applicability premise is discharged for this explicit
cone at sufficiently small selected minima. Delta=M tau, all the same-row
force identities, the unscaled parameter bounds, and the normal-preserving
ordinary limiting stress may be combined there. Exact affine composition
handles PL creases for affine nullity.

## 4. Limits of the conclusion

This proof does not admit arbitrary formal body speeds, freely change inside
allocations, prove inverse-density uniform integrability, or remove the
boundary defect in the volume martingale. It verifies a necessary structural
certificate at a hypothetical extremal family. A sharp Gamma_d/k payment from
that certificate remains unproved; this is not a complete proof of OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
